About this Event

Flow of Attraction is a gentle, heart-centered couples yoga class designed to help partners reconnect physically, emotionally, and energetically. Through mindful movement, breathwork, and intentional partner poses, couples are guided to soften into presence, deepen trust, and awaken the natural magnetism that exists between them.
This class emphasizes attunement over performance, inviting you to listen to your own body while remaining aware of your partner’s energy, boundaries, and needs. You’ll explore practices that support eye contact, synchronized breath, and conscious touch, creating space for vulnerability, playfulness, and deeper emotional intimacy.

You’ll leave feeling more connected, grounded, and aligned—carrying the resonance of shared presence beyond the mat and into your relationship.

long_description:
The event begins with a short introductory talk on Buddhism. This is followed by a guided Vajrayana Buddhist meditation. The meditation generally lasts \~20 minutes, and it is accessible and beneficial to people of all experience levels. You are welcome to stay afterwards to ask any questions or talk further.

We will have meditation cushions available, but you are welcome to bring your own if you like. Chairs can also be made available for those who need.

What Is Buddhist Meditation?

In Buddhism, meditation means "effortlessly remaining in what is". This state may be brought about by calming and holding the mind, when compassion and wisdom are realized, or by working with our bodies' energy channels and meditating on light forms of Buddhas.

About Us

Diamond Way Buddhist Center Chicago belongs to an international non-profit network of over 600 lay Diamond Way Buddhist centers of the Karma Kagyu lineage of Tibetan Buddhism, founded by Lama Ole Nydahl and under the spiritual guidance of H.H. the 17th Gyalwa Karmapa, Trinley Thaye Dorje.

Diamond Way Buddhism offers practical and effective methods to realize mind’s inherent richness for the benefit of all. With an accessible and modern style, it works with people’s confidence and desire, using every situation in life to develop fearlessness and joy. We always present a basic introduction for newcomers, and the meditations are guided in English.

To learn more about our center visit:
http://www.diamondway.org/chicago/

\*This event is free. Just come as you are and enjoy.

title: Madhuram — An Evening of Bharatanatyam
description: Madhuram — An Evening of Bharatanatyam
long_description:
About this Event

For millions of people around the world, Krishna is more than a deity—he is a friend, a teacher, a protector, and a symbol of love, wisdom, and joy. His stories, passed down through generations, reveal a figure who is at once playful and profound, human and divine.
Madhuram explores these many facets of Krishna through a selection of Bharatanatyam compositions. From the mischievous child who steals butter to the compassionate guide who offers wisdom in times of uncertainty, each piece reflects a different aspect of his enduring appeal and the emotions he evokes.
Presented by Meghana Boojala, Akshaya Rajkumar, and Krithika Shankar under the guidance of Madhumanti Varun Banerjee, this evening of dance invites audiences into a world of storytelling, music, and expression. Whether familiar with Krishna's stories or discovering them for the first time, viewers are invited to connect with the universal themes of love, devotion, courage, wonder, and grace that lie at the heart of these timeless works.

long_description:
Let's enjoy some Malaysian food at Food Terminal. This will be our first Malaysian food event and I think this is the perfect restaurant to do it at.

Food Terminal’s concept reflects Malaysia’s diverse culinary cuisine.

Food Terminal showcases a vibrant mix of Asian street food, with a special emphasis on authentic Malaysian cuisine. Its menu highlights a rich selection of dishes inspired by the bold flavors and culinary traditions of Indian and Chinese cooking. Together, these influences create a diverse and flavorful dining experience that reflects the true essence of Malaysia’s multicultural food culture.

**Food Terminal Origin Story:**
At age 15, Amy began her culinary path selling street-style noodles from a kiosk in Malaysia. Together with Howie, the duo came to the United States to pursue the American dream as entrepreneurs. Howie and Amy spent decades exploring culinary achievements, creating brands such as Top Spice and Sweet Hut.

Even after years of business accomplishments, the real satisfaction for them is not the success of the restaurants and bakeries, but the appreciation people express after tasting their food.
Inspired by the chefs’ personal cultural background, Food Terminal’s concept reflects Malaysia’s diverse culinary cuisine. Malaysian food draws influence from India, Guang Zhou, Hokkien, Teochew, and Hakka provinces due to the early 1900’s migration for tin and railroad labor demand. As such, Food Terminal’s menu features a high variety of Asian street foods with heavy emphasis on Malaysian cuisine. Food Terminal’s mission is to bring the most authentic Asian-style street taste and experience to Buford Highway.

**A Local Guide's review of Food Terminal:**
Food Terminal boasts an extensive South Asian menu, with a definite Malaysian bent, in a relaxed and informal atmosphere. The food is excellent. Some highlights include:

\- Beef Rendang: one of my favorite renditions of this complex and very flavorful West Sumatran dish
\- Chicken Satay

long_description:
Join us every Friday for **[Lunch with the Poets](https://greenmountainwriters.com/poetry/lunch-with-poets-burlington-vermont/)**, a relaxed, weekly gathering of poets, writers, readers, and lovers of language at The Innovation Café in Burlington.

Whether you write poetry, enjoy listening to it, or simply appreciate creative conversation, you're invited to pull up a chair and join us for lunch.

Participants are welcome to share a poem of their own or one they love during our open reading session, or simply sit back, enjoy lunch, and listen. No experience is required, and new faces are always welcome.

**Event Schedule**

**11:45 AM – 12:15 PM**
Lunch & Conversation

Enjoy lunch, meet fellow writers and readers, and connect with members of Vermont's creative community.

**12:15 PM – 1:00 PM**
Open Poetry Readings

Participants are invited to share one or two poems. Readings are generally limited to 3–5 minutes each so everyone has an opportunity to participate.

**1:00 PM – 1:15 PM**
Meet the Poets & Networking

Stay a little longer to continue conversations, exchange ideas, and make new connections.

**Cost**
Free to attend. Food and beverages are available for purchase from The Innovation Café.
Your RSVP will help us to arrange a group table in advance. But feel free to invite friends. Simply bring your appetite and your love of words.
We look forward to seeing you there.

**Organizer's Note:** This is intended to be a welcoming and supportive gathering rather than a formal critique group. Original work, favorite poems by other authors, and first-time readers are all welcome.

**Feeling isolated or navigating the tender terrain after a relationship ends? You are not alone.** **Join us for** **Quiet Conversations: Our Haven for Connection****, a warm and welcoming space designed for genuine support and understanding.**

**We gather bi-weekly at the Glendale Branch Library. This isn't just a meetup; it's a place to find your footing, share your journey, and build meaningful connections with others who truly understand.**

**Whether you're newly separated, years post-divorce, or simply looking to expand your supportive circle, this peer-led group offers a haven to feel seen, heard, and deeply supported.** **Please note: This is a peer-led community, not a therapy or coaching group. It's a space for shared experience and mutual encouragement, not professional mental health support.**

**Your Contribution to Our Haven:** **This community thrives on the spirit of mutual support. Many members have expressed how invaluable these gatherings are, and some have even offered to contribute financially. To help us continue providing this vital space and cover Meetup fees and other community resources, we welcome your support.**

**Suggested Donation: $10 - $20 per session (or whatever feels right for you).** **Your generosity helps us keep things going and the conversations flowing.**

**You can contribute via Venmo: @michaelleavitthwb**

**Ready to find your chosen family?** **If you're also looking for a creative outlet and a deeper dive into music and shared creativity, check out our sister community,** **[Wandering Bards](https://www.meetup.com/wanderingbard)****. It's our primary home for finding your 'shovel friends' through the power of music, storytelling, and continued growth. Explore our events and join the quest!**

long_description:
Reiki is a Japanese healing technique for stress reduction and relaxation that also promotes healing.

The term Rei is universal and connects the spiritual realms. Rei connects the Universal Consciousness / Universal Mind / God / Supreme Being with the elemental forces of the Earth through the Mind, Body and Spirit of a human being.

Ki is Life Force Energy, the same as Chi, Prana, Ti or Ki; the biofield of energy. Life Force Energy plays an important role in everything we do. Sometimes is can be misappropriated / blocked / restrained by conditions of our daily life, fluctuations of the mind or patterns both adopted from our habits and or from traumas experienced.

The human, or healer, acts as a bridge to bring Reiki wisdom, guidance and healing down to the people.

Reiki is a unique kind of Ki, it is guided by spiritual consciousness; it is brought to the student though an attunement from a Reiki Master Teacher. This attunement is an initiation of sorts; adjusting the students energy pathways to accommodate the ability to channel Reiki energy. It is held by a sacred lineage of practitioners who hold space for the ever expanding ocean of waking consciousness.

When you are attuned, you have a lifetime of awareness both ahead of you and behind you, carrying the wisdom of all who have come before you and all who will come after you. Reiki can be used for self healing, to provide a safe container to help others heal, and to lovingly honor the Great Turning, happening RIGHT NOW.

In this course you will learn about the power and support of the Usui Reiki lineage, receive the Reiki Level 1 attunement, have the opportunity to experience hands on practice / receive from fellow students, and create community for integration.

Emily’s Reiki Journey: Emily Williams has been practicing Reiki since 2015, receiving her Reiki1/2/Master attunements from Jennifer Carmack, and her Reiki Master Teacher attunements from Libby Barnett.

long_description:
##

*Along with all the usual exhibits there is a special exhibit going on now:*

***Declarative Acts and Revolutionary Actors*** features objects that fueled the revolution and unsung heroes who made independence possible. The exhibition showcases national treasures from Cincinnati Museum Center’s collections, including an original timber and chain from pre-Cincinnati’s Fort Washington, the regimental flag of the 1st Pennsylvania Battalion – one of just 30 Revolutionary War flags still in existence – ***and the document that united a nation, the Declaration of Independence. Cincinnati Museum Center’s Holt Broadside of the Declaration of Independence, dated July 9, 1776, is one of just five known to have endured the past 250 years.***

Because of its extreme scarcity and light sensitivity, it is typically kept in secure, climate-controlled archival. It will only be on display from July 3rd until August 23rd.

If not a member, tickets are $25.00 for adults, $17.50 60+ & kids. If you have a Hamilton County library card, you can also get free passes using the Discovery Pass.

Tickets Includes admission to Children's Museum, Museum of Natural History & Science, and Cincinnati History Museum.

We'll then cross the historic Roebling Suspension Bridge into Covington, arriving near Greenup Street. After exploring Covington's riverfront and downtown area, we'll return to Cincinnati along the riverfront via Theodore M. Berry Way, Freedom Way, and Race Street, finishing back at the Kinley Hotel.

**Approximate Distance & Time:**
Distance: Approximately 3 miles
Walking Time: About 1 hour 9 minutes
The walk will include several stops for conversation, storytelling, photography, and discussion, making the overall experience approximately 3 hours (10:00 AM – 1:00 PM).

long_description:
Socrates Café meets twice a month. Though this may be considered a "philosophical" group, there are no rules as to what is discussed. Usually, the topics revolve around social concerns, morality, and the first principles of things.

Prior to each meeting we vote online for the questions we will discuss. That way, we will have enough time to ruminate on them and have more in-depth conversations. If you RSVP to a meeting, you may post your question in the event comments section below. I'll send out a survey for voting a few days prior to the meetup. We discuss two questions each night. So you will get to cast two votes in the survey.

When we meet, we break into smaller groups of five to seven to discuss the top two vote-getters. Each group discusses one question for around 45-50 minutes, and we then take a short break. After reconvening, each group moves on to its second question.

Hope to see you there!

-Brian

long_description:
**India's Great Mughals: Art, Power, and Opulence**
**Immerse yourself in the golden age of the Mughal Empire. India's Great Mughals: Art, Power, and Opulence celebrates the glorious artistic achievements and grandeur of one of history's great empires.**
**India's Great Mughals includes 200 sumptuous objects—intricate paintings and manuscripts, lavish textiles, architectural elements, metalwork, furniture, arms and armor, dazzling precious stones, and more. Opulent works of art—many made in the imperial workshops—convey the power and tastes of the three most celebrated Mughal emperors: Akbar (r. 1556–1605), Jahangir (r. 1605–27), and Shah Jahan (r. 1628–58). From the tiniest jeweled objects to the monumental wonder of the Taj Mahal, this highly sophisticated and globally connected empire produced treasures of unparalleled splendor and magnificence.**

Join SUP Frederick for our annual 32-mile downriver paddle adventure on the Potomac River from Brunswick, MD to Violette’s Lock!

📆 August 1–2, 2026

Whether this is your first LONG distance paddle or you’re one of our returning 32-Miler alumni… you’ll love the challenge!

This is NOT a race; it’s a laid-back, long-distance journey down the Potomac River. We take breaks, move together, enjoy the scenery, and settle into the rhythm of the river one mile at a time. 🌊

This event is known for great people, beautiful scenery, snack breaks, stories, and a whole lot of river miles.

Paddle boards, kayaks, canoes, and adventure seekers welcome.

📍 ROUTE
Brunswick Boat Ramp → Violette’s Lock = 32 miles

🕘 DAY ONE
Meet: 8:30 AM
Launch: 9:00 AM sharp
📍 Brunswick Boat Ramp(near the MARC train station). We’ll paddle approximately 16 miles downstream on day one before camping overnight at 🏕️ Marble Quarry Hiker-Biker Campsite (one of the many first-come, first-serve campsites with fire pit + restroom access)

☕ DAY TWO
We break camp in the morning and paddle downstream to White’s Ferry (see menu here: https://www.whitesferrygrill.com) for breakfast / coffee / regroup / resupply before the final stretch to Violette’s Lock

🚣 This paddle is definitely for everybody, with so many options. You can:

• Paddle the full 32 miles with us over two days
• Paddle day one only (launch with us from Brunswick at 9:00 AM and exit at any of the boat ramps along the route).
• Join for day two only near White’s Ferry (meet us for coffee/breakfast before launching downstream with the group).
• Camp with us overnight and spend the weekend hiking or biking the C&O Canal Towpath.
• Meet up with the group anywhere along the route at one of the many launch/takeout points, just message me and I’ll give you ETA to next ramp/meeting point (reach out to me in advance).

description:

long_description:
Just east of Las Vegas lies one of Southern Nevada's most colorful and overlooked landscapes. While Lava Butte is interesting from the ground, its true beauty reveals itself from above in the morning light, where layers of red, yellow, orange, and tan hills create abstract patterns that seem more at home in a painting than the Mojave Desert.

This event is specifically designed for drone photographers looking to capture a perspective that simply can't be appreciated from ground level. We'll explore the area at a relaxed pace, searching for the best aerial compositions, colorful ridgelines, winding washes, and the unique textures that make Lava Butte such a hidden gem. Whether you're an experienced pilot or just looking to gain more flight time in a spectacular location, this is a great opportunity to photograph one of the most drone-friendly landscapes near Las Vegas.

**MEETUP INFO:**
We will meet at 6:30am at Sunrise Trailhead. This is just a 30 minute drive from Las Vegas (on the east side of the city by Wetlands Park). Please plan accordingly to arrive on time.

From there, we will drive about 20 minutes down Lava Butte Road on a gravel road that is not recommended for low clearance vehicles. However, it does not require 4WD / AWD. Carpooling is available (I personally would have room for 3 passengers).

**MEETUP FEES:**
There are no fees for this event.

**PHYSICAL ACTIVITY:**
There is minimal walking required, as we will drive into Lava Butte and be able to fly right from our vehicles. Those wishing to explore additional viewpoints may choose to walk short distances over uneven desert terrain.

**ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:**
Please ensure your drone is charged, updated, and ready to fly prior to arrival.

If your plans change and you are unable to attend, please be courteous and cancel your RSVP so that someone else can attend.

**DESERT PHOTO EXPLORERS LIABILITY DISCLAIMER AND ASSUMPTION OF RISK:**
By submitting your RSVP and participating in any Desert Photo Ex

long_description:
Hey Poetry Lovers!

This group is on a roll. Here’s the gist:

We meet at the **Capital One Café in Chinatown** from **12pm - 2pm** every other week.

For enrichment, we start by reading and reflecting on a **“published poem”**, suggested by someone in the group. No advance preparation is necessary. But feel free to check out some of the poems we’ve read [here](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/e/2PACX-1vSyE_wCLQCPHRrKmN5F9tOIeeRQUZESxjRXGVBoCF2uU8Gm0_d0uECiCBCQXEy6ksxfsBOhtRIOpW3T/pubhtml?gid=0&single=true&widget=true&headers=false%22%3E%3C/iframe%3E). Or submit suggestions for future meetings [here](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSexGc2Z2Kp6bZW0D3_hfJ7NUUkfNHf7TXX-43FglCeBd9EF2Q/viewform?usp=send_form).

Next, we **share our work and offer feedback**. Depending on attendance, everyone gets \~10 minutes to use as they like. (No need to share, though; you’re welcome to come even if you prefer just to listen.)

We maintain a **Discord server** to help share our work and communicate outside our bi-weekly meet-ups. If you haven’t used Discord before, take a moment to download it and create an account before arriving. When we meet you on Saturday, we will add you to our server, the “DC Poetry Workshop”, and can help you navigate the app if you have questions.

Finally, if you plan on sharing a poem, consider how you will do so. Some options include:

* Print 5-10 copies to distribute in person
* Take and share screenshots in the Discord chat.
* Copy the poem into a google doc, change sharing settings to “anyone with link”, and copy the google doc link into the Discord chat.

Most importantly, we’re excited to meet you!

Catch you on Saturday,

Diego / Ian / Cayden / Nate / Otasha / Lia / An

✨ **Description:** What if a walk in nature could nourish your well-being while helping others experience the healing power of the outdoors?
Join Imagine Well Being's Mindful Hiking Challenge and discover how simple acts of presence can create meaningful change- for yourself and for your community.
You'll explore beautiful landscapes, engage in mindfulness practices, and reconnect with the natural world in ways that inspire curiosity, gratitude, and wonder. Whether you hike a mountain trail, wander through a historic landscape, or pause beside a quiet stream, each step becomes an invitation to slow down, notice more deeply, and remember your connection to the living world around you.

To guide your journey, the challenge invites you to explore three distinct types of landscapes:

* **Historic Sites:** *Where we listen to the stories of the land.*
* **National Scenic Trails:** *Where the path guides us back to ourselves.*
* **National Parks:** *Where awe expands our perspective.*

⚙️ **How it Works**
You choose how, when, and where you explore. Complete the challenge at your own pace, and enrich your journey by joining our hosted, in-person community events—from hikes and bike rides to forest bathing, sound baths, and mindful movement.
📖 Participants receive a downloadable mindful hiking guide for each landscape, featuring sensory and creative invitations to explore with curiosity, deepen awareness, and discover what the land has to share.

💖 **The Impact:** A Practice of Reciprocity
Just like a healthy forest relies on an unseen network of roots to thrive, this challenge creates a beautiful cycle of mutual care between you and your community.

long_description:
After his home is destroyed and his parents are killed in the Iran-Iraq war, Bashu, a small, dark-skinned boy from the Arabic-speaking Persian Gulf region of Iran, escapes on a truck to the northern part of the country, bordering the Caspian Sea. There he is taken in by Na’i, a peasant woman raising her own two children alone because her husband, who lost an arm in the war, is elsewhere in the country seeking employment. Since Na’i speaks only Gilaki, a local tongue, she and Bashu have no language in common. But over time they form a strong bond.

[Click here to watch a short scene from the film](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JSDcbZMVo58)

long_description:
Stop by Friday for an evening of drumming, singing, and meditation!

Bring your own drum or use one of ours - no experience needed!

There will be loose guidance of a rhythmic drumming session, weaving in contemporary kirtan to inspire singing and dancing.

This is a donation-based gathering-pay what you can, with a suggested contribution of $15.

**🌿 About The Karma House**
The Karma House isn’t your average bar — we’re an alcohol-free kava bar and community hub in Lakewood, CO. Our space was created to bring people together through music, art, wellness, and connection. From live shows to poetry nights to wellness workshops, everything we do centers around community and creating a safe, welcoming atmosphere for all.
**🥥 What is a Kava Bar?**
Kava bars are unique gathering places where people come to connect and unwind without alcohol. Instead of cocktails, we serve traditional Polynesian kava — a calming root tea that has been used for centuries in the South Pacific for relaxation, stress relief, and social connection.
**🍵 What is Kava?**
Kava is made from the root of the Piper methysticum plant. It has gentle, grounding effects that can help calm the body and quiet the mind, making it perfect for relaxing, connecting, and enjoying good company. At The Karma House, we prepare our shells of kava with care and community in mind — it’s more than a drink, it’s a ritual of connection.

long_description:
Join our group for a guided meditation!

The event begins with a short introductory talk on Buddhism. This is followed by a guided Vajrayana Buddhist meditation. The meditation generally lasts \~20 minutes, and it is accessible and beneficial to people of all experience levels. You are welcome to stay afterwards to ask any questions or talk further.

We will have meditation cushions available, but you are welcome to bring your own if you like. Chairs can also be made available for those who need them.

What Is Buddhist Meditation?

In Buddhism, meditation means "effortlessly remaining in what is". This state may be brought about by calming and holding the mind, when compassion and wisdom are realized, or by working with our bodies' energy channels and meditating on light forms of Buddhas.

About Us

Diamond Way Buddhist Center Chicago belongs to an international non-profit network of over 600 lay Diamond Way Buddhist centers of the Karma Kagyu lineage of Tibetan Buddhism, founded by Lama Ole Nydahl and under the spiritual guidance of H.H. the 17th Gyalwa Karmapa, Trinley Thaye Dorje.

Diamond Way Buddhism offers practical and effective methods to realize mind’s inherent richness for the benefit of all. With an accessible and modern style, it works with people’s confidence and desire, using every situation in life to develop fearlessness and joy. We always present a basic introduction for newcomers, and the meditations are guided in English.

To learn more about our center visit:
http://www.diamondway.org/chicago/

\*This event is free. Just come as you are and enjoy.

long_description:
Are you searching for a deeper sense of peace, joy, and meaning — no matter what's happening around you? 

You are warmly invited to the annual Self-Realization Fellowship World Convocation, a free weeklong immersion in the Kriya Yoga meditation teachings of Paramahansa Yogananda, author of the best-selling spiritual classic, Autobiography of a Yogi. To register, please visit convocation.yogananda.org.

Join us in Los Angeles or online from August 2–8, for:

Guided meditations to help you experience inner stillness firsthandInspirational talks on Paramahansa Yogananda’s timeless wisdom and the ancient science of yogaKirtan — uplifting devotional chantingSatsangas — informal spiritual discussionsPilgrimage tours (in-person and virtual) of Self-Realization Fellowship temples, meditation gardens, and other sacred sites established by Yogananda throughout Southern CaliforniaSome of this year’s talks include:The Art of Joyful Living: Yoga's Path to HappinessEternal Youth: What Does It Mean and How Can We Have It?Becoming an Instrument of Divine Love Inner Security Through Divine Connection

People of all faiths and backgrounds are welcome, whether you are new to meditation, have practiced for many years, or are simply interested in learning more. Convocation is an opportunity to connect with others seeking greater peace, joy, and meaning, and to take part in a worldwide spiritual community. Online tours, meditations, and talks will be simultaneously translated and available in German, Italian, Spanish, and Portuguese.

Established by Yogananda in 1950, the annual Self-Realization Fellowship Convocation is for anyone drawn to meditation, inner growth, and a deeper understanding of life’s purpose.

Self-Realization Fellowship is the international nonprofit spiritual organization founded in 1920 by Paramahansa Yogananda to introduce to people of all races, cultures, and creeds the ancient science and philosophy of yoga and its time-honored tradition of meditation. For more

long_description:
Curious about arm balances but not sure where to begin? Or looking to refine your technique and build confidence? Take Flight is a playful, alignment-focused workshop designed to make arm balances feel more accessible for every body.

Join Zion Well instructor Katie Palmer to explore the foundational principles of Crow (Bakasana) and Side Crow (Parsva Bakasana) through progressive, supportive sequencing. You'll learn how to develop hand and wrist strength, improve thoracic mobility and rotation, and understand the mechanics that create lift—without relying on brute strength.

Come ready to move, laugh, experiment, and discover that taking flight is less about perfection and more about finding balance, curiosity, and trust.

organizer: Firecraft Northwest Nature Bushcraft and Survival Outings
long_description:
During this hands-on workshop you’ll make your own basket from foraged Ponderosa Pine needles and a hand-made wooden base!
We’ll discuss how to identify the correct species for harvesting needles, when and how to harvest, and honorable and sustainable harvesting practices. Choose from multiple thread colors and wooden bases (unfinished, walnut oil finished or adorned with pressed flower) to add your own creative touch to your basket. Then, you’ll learn how to prepare your pine needles for basketry, practice multiple different stitches, understand and practice shaping walls, and learn about how to finish and seal your basket. We’ll finish the session with an overview of resources available to keep practicing on your own! Pine needle basketry is a slow and consistent craft, similar to knitting, crocheting, and embroidery - it requires a bit of patience and practice, but can be a very meditative and rewarding experience once you get the hang of it!
Please bring with you:

* A plastic bag or tupperware for transporting your basket home
* A plastic bag for taking home handfuls of soaked pine needles (gallon ziplock or larger)
* A hand towel
* Scissors
* Journal and pen for taking notes (optional)
* Mug/thermos for tea (optional)
* Water/snack (optional)
* Pliers (optional)
* Sit pad or camp chair for comfort (optional)

Register on Meetup or directly on our website to avoid a Meetup fee - https://www.firecraftnw.com/register/p/pine-needle-basketry-workshop-aug-2

What to wear?

No need to bother with super expensive designer yoga gear- just wear comfy clothes that move with you and provide decent coverage! No shoes are worn during yoga. Shoes aren’t even worn in the room where we practice yoga- so please take your shoes off at the door and leave them on a provided shoe rack or cubby.

Water?

Bring your refillable water bottle to fill up on free filtered water at the studio, or you can use one of our cups. Drink plenty of water after your class to help flush out toxins released from muscles and organs during class. As an expression of your yoga practice, you may wish to extend your gratitude to this fluid of life as you drink it up!

Storage of stuff?

Please store your personal items in provided “cubbies” inside the studio practice rooms (please don’t leave things outside the yoga room, especially valuables. And please remember to turn your cell phone off!

Food?

You might be uncomfortable during class if you just ate. So avoid eating during the two hours prior to class. You can also adopt a yogic diet that is vegetarian and energizing for maximum comfort and benefit.

long_description:
Step away from the noise and settle into an afternoon of reflection, music, and meaningful conversation.

Sounds of Wisdom is a unique contemplative experience that blends the soothing sounds of the handpan with nature-inspired soundscapes, thought-provoking monologues, guided meditations, and selected excerpts from Jaxon Phoenix’s book Only Us, designed to encourage presence, curiosity, and inner peace.

As the music unfolds, you’ll be invited to relax with a warm cup of tea or coffee, allowing the gentle rhythms of the handpan and the reflections woven throughout the experience to create space for stillness, insight, and self-discovery.

This is not a lecture, and it is not a concert. It is a gathering for those who long to slow down, think deeply, and reconnect with themselves and the world around them.

Whether you’re seeking inspiration, clarity, or simply a peaceful place to breathe, Sounds of Wisdom offers an opportunity to pause and listen—not only to the music, but to the wisdom that often emerges in moments of quiet contemplation.

Stay afterward for tea, conversation, and signed copies of Only Us, available for purchase following the event.

Come comfortable. Bring an open mind. Leave feeling grounded, refreshed, and inspired.

long_description:
**This is a Free Event.**

View a video of Darshan [here](https://youtu.be/xcZMXqBt9IU?si=ajt5Se9s1uQGRONy).

Experience Your Divine Presence Through an Intimate Moment with an Enlightened Master

As a master Sai Maa offers Darshan, an ancient Sanskrit word meaning “in the sight of the divine,” with a plume of peacock feathers, gently touching a participant’s heart and head.

**Darshan** is an intimate experience of divine presence brought about through a moment shared with an enlightened master. The master looks upon you, seeing your divinity and wholeness, and calls it forth – leading you from darkness to light.

“There’s nothing more beautiful in this world than a human being,” says Sai Maa whose name means Divine Mother. “No monument, no church; so allow yourself to be loved and you will experience yourself.

Darshan activates the divine presence that is dormant in every human being,” she adds. “The more you receive Darshan, the best of you, the divinity in you, comes to the surface.”

**Who should receive Darshan?**

Simply put, everyone. There is no one too old, too small, too angry, too lost to benefit from Darshan. You do not need to be a student of Sai Maa or follow any religion to receive the full power of Maa’s love. You don’t even need to believe in God. There is no dogma you need to know or follow. If you have a heartbeat, you can receive Darshan.

title: prAna Summer Series Yoga Class with Gaby
description: The first in a series of three special classes with guest instructor Gaby Maldonado
long_description:
The first in a series of three special classes with guest instructor Gaby Maldonado

About this Event

Gaby Maldonado is a yoga and wellness facilitator who combines her background in health psychology with ancient yogic teachings to bring awareness, healing, and mindfulness to students around the globe. As a former athlete and a traumatic brain injury survivor, Gaby has a unique ability to meet individuals where they currently are and create a yoga practice specific to them. Originally from Mt. Hood, Oregon, she has practiced yoga since childhood and taught professionally for the past 12 years. She continues to travel the world to share her offerings with countless communities and cultures, both in English and Spanish. Empire Builders Mastermind (Growth Strategies) group is hosted by International Success Coach Misty Rose Gold. Knowing that you are not alone is half the battle. When challenges arise we use our collective knowledge to create a solution. **Overview:** This practical session guides attendees through the Microsoft Fabric IQ interface: exploring workspaces, semantic models, and how ontologies are surfaced within the platform. We'll connect a sample dataset to a semantic layer, define key business entities and relationships, and demonstrate how Fabric IQ uses that ontological context to generate richer, more accurate insights. No prior Fabric experience required. You'll leave with a foundational understanding of how to begin structuring your own organization's knowledge model.

**Speaker**: Dean Jurecic is a solutions engineer and consultant who specializes in Microsoft Fabric and Power BI. He has worked with Power BI and Fabric in a variety of industries including utilities, retail, construction, government and education. Dean is an active member of the data community, a Microsoft Fabric Certified Data Engineer and Analytics Engineer Associate and a 3x Fabric Community Super User.

**Sponsor:** For almost 20 years, Wiiisdom has helped customers by providing first-class Analytics Governance Solutions that enable organizations to automate their analytics operations. The Wiiisdom Cloud Platform for Power BI and Tableau consists of 3 modules: Continuous Certification, Lifecycle Management and Predictive Monitoring that are designed to help you move from reactively to proactively managing your analytics estate.

description: A safe space for survivors of sexual violence to experience the healing benefits of Yoga. Led by Dana Perry Kirchoff, E-RYT. Hosted by CRCC.
long_description:
A safe space for survivors of sexual violence to experience the healing benefits of Yoga. Led by Dana Perry Kirchoff, E-RYT. Hosted by CRCC.

About this Event

Cleveland Rape Crisis Center invites survivors of rape and sexual abuse to a free community yoga class. This class is designed to be a safe space for survivors to experience the healing benefits of Yoga. This practice will allow students an opportunity to increase body awareness in support of greater physical, emotional and mental well being.
We will explore breathing practices and therapeutic movement to help survivors in connecting mindfully to the moment. We will learn ways to listen to our bodies and breath so we can honor our own unique experience and needs.

Who can attend?
Survivors of sexual violence/sexual trauma.All yoga experience levels welcome.All genders welcome.Survivors ages 13-17 may attend if accompanied by a parent/guardian. Please register the adult and child separately.

About Dana:
Dana has been practicing and teaching yoga for 20 years. She has trained in a variety of modalities and has learned from many amazing teachers over the years. Her most recent work has been focused on teaching yoga + mindfulness to kids ages K-8, as well as providing Trauma Informed Yoga classes for the community.
“I am deeply committed to this path and am grateful for the opportunity to share all the beautiful healing benefits these practices can provide. Along with my work in schools and as a trauma informed yoga teacher, I am also a mother and musician. I am passionate about creating communities that can support and uplift us all.”

long_description:
You have your business cards in hand and a smile on your face. You look nice, ready to share your business needs with a room full of successful entrepreneurs.

The meeting is called to order and you're asked to put your business cards away. You frown and turn to the person who invited you, “I thought this was a networking group?!” He smiles, “No, it's not. This is the Eliances community, the only place "Where Entrepreneurs Align.” Confused, you put your cards in your bag, wondering what exactly is in store for the rest of the morning.

Eliances is not a networking group; period. As the community director states, “If you're here hoping to ‘machine gun' your cards all over the room, you're in the wrong place. If you're interested in giving what you got and making real relationships, Eliances is for you.” As each entrepreneur goes around the room, sharing the “Got, Give, Get” of their business, connections begin to form and lives are changed.

“I am truly impressed with the open environment you and your team have created at Eliances. From one meeting I have already identified 2-3 potential partnership opportunities, as well as made some great connections for building relationships in the future" - expressed Kneko Burney who has been a featured guest on CNBC's the Closing Bell.

Eliances the only place "Where Entrepreneurs Align". At the weekly ROUNDtable (which changes every week of those who attend), the best minds in the entrepreneur world bring their expertise and rolodex to align with individuals with something amazing to give. Connections are made and business gets done every week as a result of these meetings. Networking groups don't do that. Stated another person who attended.

“I'm so proud of everything that you guys are doing to make a difference in people's lives” states another Eliancer.

Twice a year, the GRANDtable brings together a large group of passionate entrepreneurs, looking for their next business partner. Projects get funded, introductions are mad

long_description:
Here's the agenda for this Meetup:

Please note we will start promptly at 12:00 pm. Please be a few minutes early so you will have time to order some lunch. Also, give yourself a few minutes to catch up with other members. This will ensure that we can start on time and then we will be able to leave on time.

We do ask that as we get back to in-person networking, you WILL NEED to buy lunch to support Rock Bottom, there will also be a $1 restaurant service fee (that is NOT part of the gratuity) added to all checks.

• We'll do a brief introduction of ABNG and also quickly go over our rules (don't worry, there's only three and a half!). Then, we'll get right to the meeting.

• Hold on to your business cards for now. We will start the meeting by going around the room with our introductions. Notice we didn't say 30-second commercial or elevator pitch. There's a fantastic TED talk (https://youtu.be/u4ZoJKF_VuA) from Simon Sinek that might blow you away.

• After introductions, we'll do our shoutouts and share our member events. If you had a great 1:1 with someone or have some other awesome thing to share, we have the space for that! If you have a workshop, class, meeting or event coming up, this is a great time to inform the group. We will also discuss specific needs you may have. Do you need a resource of some kind? Chances are someone in our group can point you in the right direction.

• If time allows, we will engage in our Mastermind discussion. If you feel like you have something in your business that is holding you back, this is time and the place to tackle it. If you have something that you need help with, make sure to let the host know before the meeting starts so that we can make time for it during our meeting. The power of the group is immense!

• We'll close out our meeting by passing around business cards and ensuring you have time to set up your 1:1's before adjourning at 1:00 p.m.

We look forward to seeing you at our next meeting!

long_description:
The Delivery Fellowship invites design and product professionals to an interactive session on turning design work into clear, compelling stories. Led by Noel Childs, the evening will explore how stronger storytelling can help designers communicate decisions, connect with audiences, and build influence.

**Date:** Wednesday, August 5, 2026
**Location:** Institute of Design, Illinois Institute of Technology
**Address:** 3137 S. Federal Street, Chicago, IL 60616

**Event Schedule**
**5:30 PM** — Doors open for networking, drinks, and refreshments
**6:00 PM** — Presentation begins
**6:30 PM** — Interactive workshop begins
**7:00 PM** — Small-group presentations and feedback
**7:30 PM** — Event concludes, followed by optional drinks at a nearby restaurant

**Key objectives we'll explore**

* Structure design presentations around the audience, problem, decisions, and outcome.
* Explain complex design work without overwhelming people with unnecessary details.
* Present ideas with greater clarity, confidence, and influence.

**Interactive workshop**
Participants will apply the concepts from the presentation to shape and practice a concise story about design work. You will collaborate in small groups, test your approach, and receive constructive feedback.

* Choose a project, concept, or design decision to present.
* Build a focused narrative with a clear beginning, middle, and conclusion.
* Practice presenting your story and gather feedback from other participants.

**What you'll leave with**
You will leave with a practical approach for developing stronger design narratives and presenting your work more effectively to clients, leaders, and cross-functional teams.

* A repeatable framework for structuring design stories.
* Greater confidence explaining your process and decisions.
* Practical feedback you can apply to future presentations.

long_description:
**AIMUG Monthly Mixer & Showcase**
**Austin LangChain + AI Middleware Users Group**
**Time:** 6:00 PM – 8:30 PM
**Venue:** ACC – RGC 3000, 1218 West Avenue, Austin, TX
**After-Party:** The Tavern, 922 W 12th St, Austin, TX

***

**Quick Summary**
Join us for the monthly AIMUG Mixer & Showcase — an evening of practical demos, short deep-dives, and relaxed community networking.
We focus on **agentic software development**: multi-agent architectures, middleware patterns, **LangChain + LangGraph** workflows, **DeepAgents**, and real-world a**pplication building**.
Many presenters are power users of **Claude Code**, and we frequently explore how developers use it in their agent workflows.

***

**Run of Show (Template / Reusable)**
**6:00 – 6:20 PM — Networking & Welcome**
Grab a drink, meet other AI practitioners, settle in.
**6:20 – 6:30 PM — Introductions & Kickoff (10 min)**
Brief community intros + overview of the agenda.
**6:30 – 7:40 PM — Thunderstorm Talks (15 min each)**

* **Thunderstorm Talk Slot 1 (15 min)**
* **Thunderstorm Talk Slot 2 (15 min)**
* **Thunderstorm Talk Slot 3 (15 min)**
* **Thunderstorm Talk Slot 4 (15 min)**

**7:40 – 8:00 PM — Buffer & Open Q&A**
Follow up with speakers, demo projects, or run long if needed.
*Target wrap-up: \~7:45–8:00 PM; venue clears by 8:30 PM.*
**8:00 – 8:30 PM — Walk to After-Party**
Casual mixer continues at **The Tavern**.

***

**About AIMUG**
AIMUG is built on the philosophy of **Learning in the Open**.
We explore the entire agentic stack — LangChain, LangGraph, LangSmith, DeepAgents, Claude Code, Claude Skills/Subagents, and the broader AI middleware ecosystem.
Expect demos, patterns, pitfalls, and community-built insights from developers shipping real agent-powered applications.
We’re graciously hosted by the Center for Government & Civic Service at ACC’s Rio Grande Campus.

***

long_description:
Hosted by: Ngakpa International & the Buddhist Studies Institute

Explore the path of Vajrayana and Great Perfection (Dzogchen)

Online classes, meeting twice a month, students will discover how to understand the pivotal principles of Tibetan Buddhism, make sense of empowerments, and go deep into understanding oneself, one’s own world, and how to make better sense of one’s own mind.

Vajrayana Training is offered in modules. The courses are non-sequential and can be taken in any order.

The Classes generally include a 30-minute lecture by Pema Khandro followed by 30-minutes discussion.

-fuel your inspiration
-discover your hidden depths
-immerse yourself in dharma
-connect with other Buddhists
-cut through fictions to see yourself as you really are
-understanding your mind and emotions
-gain support for ongoing practice and study
-clarify the meaning of esoteric Buddhist philosophy, terms and rituals
-engage Buddhist philosophy to grapple with the issue of teacher student relationships in Vajrayana
-leave behind the maze of information and have a direct encounter with the heart of Buddhism

What is Vajrayana?

Vajrayana is a Buddhist path for utilizing our life experiences as the fuel for the path. Vajrayana is a system of practices to cultivate a wakeful clear presence and connect with goodness in ourselves and others.

In Vajrayana ordinary life experiences become the focal point for our training. Vajrayana refers to a path of “transformation” of these experiences. It is the transformation of thinking, experiencing emotions, embodied experience, visualization, identity, moments of crisis, dreaming and dying into opportunities for connecting with intrinsic wisdom.

The view of the world in Vajrayana is that innate wisdom and potential for awakening is always present. Through Vajrayana meditation practices and Buddhist philosophy, we train to see the world with a “pure view,” an openness to connect with what is good, uplifted, the positive potential. title: Yoga for Rhonda: A Donation-Based Class Benefiting Head for the Cure
description: Join us for an outdoor sunset all-levels yoga class honoring Rhonda Trosen and supporting Head for the Cure through optional donations.
long_description:
Join us for an outdoor sunset all-levels yoga class honoring Rhonda Trosen and supporting Head for the Cure through optional donations.

About this Event

Donation-Based Community Outdoor Yoga for Head for the Cure
Join us for a special outdoor yoga class honoring the life and legacy of Rhonda Trosen. This class is open to all levels, with 100% of donations benefiting Head for the Cure, supporting brain cancer research and families affected by brain tumors.
In Loving Memory of Rhonda: My name is Bethany Lang, co-owner of YogaSix St. Louis.
I'm hosting this class in memory of my best friend's mom, Rhonda Trosen.
Rhonda was an incredible grandmother, mother, wife, friend, Tri Sigma sister, Truman State alumna, and so much more. Above all, she had an extraordinary gift for making everyone feel seen, valued, and loved. Whether it was a handwritten card, a thoughtful text, or simply remembering the little things that mattered, she made everyone around her feel special.
After Rhonda's courageous battle with brain cancer, I wanted to create a space where our community could come together to honor her life while supporting others facing this disease.
If you're able, please consider making a donation to Head for the Cure in Rhonda's honor. Every contribution, no matter the amount, helps fund brain cancer research and provide support to families navigating a brain tumor diagnosis.
Thank you for helping us celebrate Rhonda's beautiful legacy through movement, community, and giving back.
Donations: Suggested $10. Donations will be accepted via Eventbrite or on-site cash/Venmo. All proceeds from this event will be donated to Head for the Cure in Rhonda's memory.
Class Details:
Check-in: 7:00pm
Class: 7:30-8:30pm
What to bring: yoga mat, towel, water bottle (option cash or Venmo for donation on site) Class will be OUTDOORS, please plan to dress appropriately (sunscreen/bugspray)
Location: Class will be held in the grassy courtyard space by the courtyard/fountain. NO NEED TO CHECK

title: Rest, Restore, Resist: A Restorative Yoga Series for Black Women
description: This three week restorative yoga series is specifically designed to address the intersectional stress Black women face on a daily basis.
long_description:
This three week restorative yoga series is specifically designed to address the intersectional stress Black women face on a daily basis.

About this Event

Rest, Restore Resist, is a three week restorative yoga series that has been curated for Black Women by Dr. Ashley A. Hicks (RYT200 and licensed therapist)
This series begins on Wednesday August 5th and continues though August 19th weekly from 6:30pm - 8pm ET. 
Join us in a small and intimate setting and experience the healing benefits of restorative yoga. Each session will last for 75 minutes and include supportive physical postures, breathwork, meditation, and reiki (optional). All yoga mats and props will be provied.
This series creates a space for Black women to rest in community and provides an opportunity for us to address the unique intersectional stressors we face on a daily basis. This workshop is influenced by the work of Rest Is Resistance by Tricia Hersey and Restorative Yoga for Ethnic and Race-Based Stress and Trauma by Dr. Gail Parker.

Payment is based on a pay what you can scale to make this work accessible to as many women as possible.
Payment options
1) Receive - $30 for the full series ( $10/class)
2) Contribute - $45 for the full series ($15/class)
3) Sustain - $60 for the full series ($20/class)

This workshop is a part of Ashley's 300-hour yoga practicum required to achieve an RYT-500 certification.
Join us as we rest. Rest is our birthright. Let's rest now!

Also check out other Health & Wellness events in Columbus, Workshops in Columbus.

Each session of community yoga at Urban Park will be led by a friendly instructor from our neighborhood Corepower Yoga. This series is open to people of all skill levels! Make sure to bring your yoga mat and a water bottle! 
Registration for the June 3 class will open May 29 at 10AM. The only way to register is via Eventbrite. Registration for the remaining classes in the series will open at the end of the class prior. 
As space is limited for these classes, please cancel your registration  if you can no longer attend, and do so a minimum of 1 hour prior to the class start. long_description:
Sacred Dialogs is a guided inquiry circle exploring the spiritual philosophy of the Bhagavad Gītā as a foundational yoga text (Yoga Śāstra) and a practical guide for conscious living.
Rather than a lecture format, the session uses Community of Inquiry methods inspired by philosopher Matthew Lipman, creating a respectful, thoughtful space where participants explore questions together.

Topics may include:
• Purpose and meaning in yogic life
• The nature of the self and consciousness
• Action, intention, and inner freedom
• Applying yoga wisdom to modern daily life

Participants are encouraged to listen deeply, reflect honestly, and share at their own comfort level. No philosophical background is required—curiosity and openness are enough.
Each gathering concludes with a wholesome vegetarian dinner, allowing conversation to continue informally while fostering warmth, connection, and community.

long_description:
NAMI Connection Recovery Support Group is a free, peer-led support group for any adult who has experienced symptoms of a mental health condition. You will gain insight from hearing the challenges and successes of others, and the groups are led by trained leaders who’ve been there.
NAMI’s support groups are unique because they follow a structured model to ensure you and others in the group have an opportunity to be heard and to get what you need.

* Free of cost to participants
* Designed for adults (18+) with mental health conditions
* Led by people with mental health conditions
* 90 minutes long and meets weekly, every other week or monthly (varies by location)
* No specific medical therapy or treatment is endorsed
* Confidential

\#\# What You’ll Gain
By sharing your experiences in a safe and confidential setting, you can gain hope and feel a sense of connection. The group encourages empathy, productive discussion and a sense of community. You’ll benefit from other’s experiences, discover your inner strength and empower yourself by sharing your own experiences in a non-judgmental space.
NAMI Connection Recovery Support Group will help you:

* Aim for better coping skills
* Find strength in sharing experiences
* Not judge anyone’s pain
* Forgive ourselves and reject guilt
* Embrace humor as healthy
* Accept that we cannot solve every problem
* Understand that mental health conditions are no one’s fault and can be traumatic experiences

long_description:
**The Art of Hands-On Adjustments & Assists**

Join us for an informative and experiential workshop designed for yoga teachers, teacher trainees, and dedicated students who wish to deepen their understanding of hands-on adjustments and assists. Rooted in the traditions of Astāṅga Yoga, skillful adjustments can help students experience greater alignment, stability, awareness, and ease within a posture while supporting the development of a safe and effective practice.

This workshop will explore the principles behind effective assisting, including proper body mechanics, communication, observation skills, and the distinction between adjusting, assisting, and supporting. Participants will learn how to assess individual needs, apply appropriate levels of pressure and guidance, and offer adjustments that enhance rather than force a posture.
We will work through a wide range of postures from the standing, seated, and reclining sequences, as well as techniques for supporting students in relaxation and Śavāsana. Emphasis will be placed on maintaining the integrity of the pose, honoring individual differences, and cultivating confidence and sensitivity as an assistant.
Whether you are a teacher looking to refine your hands-on skills or a student curious about the role of adjustments in yoga practice, this workshop will provide practical tools, hands-on experience, and a deeper appreciation for the art of assisting others on the yoga path.

\*Yoga Alliance YACEP accredited hours available

long_description:
Come out and join us for this exciting talk by Ben, and networking during the meetup and at the Burns Pub afterward.

Food will be sponsored by Sovereign this month. Learn more about sovereign at [https://sovereign.trading](https://sovereign.trading).

\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-

TL;DR: This talk is a primer for `std::execution`. Not just recipes, but understanding the computational model of senders.

C++26 adds senders to `std::execution`: a major feature that gives us tools for defining and composing asynchronous work. This talk will look at parts of `std::execution` and explain how they work, and how they map on to computational ideas.

We will deconstruct the ideas of execution; see how the familiar synchronous model fits in; see how the asynchronous model generalizes it; and get an understanding of how to build back up into anything we need. We'll cover all the major new parts of `std::execution`, and see the designs behind what ships in C++26 and where they might be fleshed out in future.

C++ has long been considered a low-level language in the sense of "close to the hardware". Now, arguably, it is finally becoming a low(er)-level language in a computational sense.

\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-

There is a discord for the meetup that you can join https://discord.gg/98T5XPWcrA to help foster remote interaction!
We always plan to go to the Burns pub for social hour after the presentation.

\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-

long_description:
**Sierra Club and Beer: Traveling through the Ages at Petroglyph National Monument**

*Sign up @ https://www.riograndesierraclub.org/calendar/*

Petroglyph National Monument, encompassing Albuquerque's West Mesa, encapsulates the human and environmental experiences from upwards of 20 million years ago to the present. With over 24,000 petroglyphs, primarily inscribed by the ancestors of modern Puebloan Peoples, the national monument preserves one of largest concentrations of petroglyphs in the world along with the desolate New Mexican High Desert's beauty.

This presentation, from Petroglyph National Monument's Community Volunteer Ambassador, Wes Reinig, is intended to highlight the incredible geology, environment, Ancestral Puebloan and Spanish culture and lifestyles that has dramatically changed over the course of the Albuquerque Area's rich and lengthy history. The importance of this monument operated by the National Park Service and City of Albuquerque is an ode to the land's historic usage and appearance in contrast with the rapid development of Albuquerque.

Come enjoy drinks and snacks with likeminded friends. RSVP at
*Sign up @ https://www.riograndesierraclub.org/calendar/*

The meeting will be held at St. Mark’s Episcopal Church, 431 Richmond Place NE, Albuquerque, from 7:00 p.m. to 8:30 p.m.

long_description:
In one of the most important and beloved Latin American works of the twentieth century, Isabel Allende weaves a luminous tapestry of three generations of the Trueba family, revealing both triumphs and tragedies. Here is patriarch Esteban, whose wild desires and political machinations are tempered only by his love for his ethereal wife, Clara, a woman touched by an otherworldly hand. Their daughter, Blanca, whose forbidden love for a man Esteban has deemed unworthy infuriates her father, yet will produce his greatest joy: his granddaughter Alba, a beautiful, ambitious girl who will lead the family and their country into a revolutionary future.

long_description:
There are evenings that stay with you long after the last note has faded.
This is one of them.

Join us for an evening of Hindustani classical vocal music with **Swati Jhaveri** — a journey through ragas that span the breadth of human emotion, from the profound and contemplative to the tender and joyful.
The program moves through the classical tradition with intention and heart: from the weight of a full-throated khayal to the playful intimacy of a thumri, and culminating in an original composition that reflects Swati's own voice within the lineage she carries.

Trained in the Indore and Mewati gharana traditions, Swati brings to the stage a rare ability to hold depth and warmth in equal measure.

She will be accompanied by **Tushar Gupte on tabla** and **Satyam Bagwe on harmonium**.

An evening of music in its most honest form.

**Swati Jhaveri** pursues music with a deep passion. She is currently under the guidance of Pandit Hemang Mehta (disciple of Padma Vibhushan Pandit Jasraj and Pandit Chandrasekhar Swamy) of the Mewati Gharana and Vidushi Kankana Banerjee of the Indore and Mewati Gharana (disciple of Ustad Amir Khan Sahib and Pandit Pratap Narayan) as part of the guru shishya parampara.

Swati started learning music at the age of 4 and has had the opportunity to study with many learned gurus including Pandit Pratap Narayan, Pandit Askaran Sharma, and Pandit Sougata Banerjee.

She started a non profit called “Swara Institute for Music Research and Appreciation” with the purpose of improving the reach of Indian Classical music through teaching, content creation, and supporting under-privileged, retired, and upcoming musicians.

Swati has produced a series of classical singles with a contemporary touch on popular platforms, in an attempt to make classical music palatable to wider masses and our younger generation.

title: Mangini Ranch Meditation Hike
description: Mangini Ranch Meditation Hike
long_description:
Join Save Mount Diablo on a meditation journey through Mangini Ranch!

About this Event

Beat the summer heat on this early morning outing on Mangini Ranch. Save Mount Diablo’s 208-acre property includes the headwaters of Galindo Creek with rolling grasslands, oaks, buckeyes, and a rare desert olive grove. Visit a secret spring and keep your eyes out; you might see bobcats and coyotes looking for breakfast, plus burrowing owls, quail, and many other feathered friends who are active in the morning. This is a two-hour hike with one strenuous climb. Three to five short meditations will be offered during the hike. Be sure to dress in layers and wear sturdy boots or shoes; bring plenty of water and a snack. Restrooms not available. Heavy rain cancels.
Participant Limit: 20 people
Land: Save Mount Diablo’s Mangini Ranch Educational Preserve
Rating: Easy/Moderate
Distance: 3 miles
Elevation change: 300 feet
Leader: Jim & Sharon Lawrence, Save Mount Diablo Volunteer Hike Leaders

Directions: From Ygnacio Valley Road, turn south on Crystyl Ranch Drive in Concord. Continue on Crystyle Ranch Drive for one and a half miles until you reach the hiker gate next to 5318 Crystyl Ranch Drive on the south side of the street.

Anyone under the age of 18 will need to be accompanied by a parent or guardian.

You might bring a Chinese news article for us to read together, tell a story, teach us about a holiday or cultural tradition, share a favorite song, demonstrate a hobby, explain a grammar point, introduce new vocabulary, play a game, or teach us something completely unique, all in Chinese.

The goal is not to be a perfect teacher. It is to practice Chinese in a relaxed, supportive environment while learning from one another. Everyone has unique experiences, interests, and knowledge that can help the group grow.

Whether you come to teach, learn, or both, you will leave having practiced your Chinese in a meaningful and engaging way.

All levels are welcome. Bring your curiosity, your creativity, and something you would love to share. I'm excited to learn from you! I'll bring something short to share as well. Feel free to bring snacks for the group! ❤️

If this event goes well and gets enough attendees I'll hold it once a month. 謝謝！

long_description:
Space is limited to 12. Please use this link to save your spot...[Sign me up!](https://forms.gle/xY3kf9ERwgAD7ptu8)

Let Your Fascia Flow is a 2 hour workshop incorporating Self-Myofascial Release techniques and Yoga to release tension, alleviate pain, and improve mobility.

Why Fascia Matters: Fascia is a web-like connective tissue that surrounds every muscle, bone, organ, and nerve and gives the body support and structure. It can be affected by physical injuries as well as our emotions. Physical injuries, surgeries and emotional strain in the body can lead to adhesions in the fascia which cause tightness, discomfort, pain and restricted movement.

Why you will love this workshop: Through targeted pressure, intentional movement and breath work, self-myofascial release aids in reducing fascial adhesions and tension, eases pain while promoting better movement throughout your entire body. Maintaining our mobility and range of motion is one of the keys to aging gracefully.

Perfect for you if: you're an athlete, weekend warrior, navigating mid-life changes, experiencing chronic tension, or simply looking to improve your overall well-being.

No previous yoga experience is required, just bring your curiosity and willingness to try something new!

What you will experience:

Guided self-myofascial release techniques using therapy balls and massage balls.
A series of yoga poses designed to stretch and open the body
Breath work and mindfulness to support relaxation and healing
Personalized adjustments to address your unique needs

Leave feeling lighter, more mobile, and deeply connected to your body.

Investment $40
Please use link above to register.

A 90 min experience designed to help you regulate your nervous system, deepen your capacity for connection, and leave feeling grounded.

About this Event

ATUNE: Nervous System Training & Sound BathConnection is not just emotional.
It is physiological.
When the nervous system is under strain, it becomes harder to feel calm, open, safe, and present. Many of us are trying to connect, heal, and function well from bodies that have not fully learned how to come out of stress.
ATUNE: Nervous System Training & Sound Bath is a guided experience designed to help you begin changing that.
You’re invited a 90 minute immersive experience that combines nervous system education, embodied regulation, and restorative sound to help you return to yourself.
Together, we’ll explore what it means to regulate from the inside out — not just intellectually, but somatically.
You’ll leave with:
a clearer understanding of nervous system dysregulationa felt experience of grounding and restorationpractical tools to support greater calm and emotional capacitya deeper sense of connection to your body and breathThis is not about forcing calm.
It is about training for connection.
Training for capacity.
Training for a more regulated way of being.
Come if you’ve been craving a reset.
Come if your body has been carrying too much.
Come if you’re ready for a deeper kind of exhale.
Kindred Healing Center ( near Black Coffee Company)
Atlanta, GA
Limited capacity

organizer: Come Sit With Us - A Meditation and Community Group
long_description:
Join us for a special community screening of *One Track Heart: The Story of Krishna Das*, followed by a conversation with director Jeremy Frindel.

The film follows the journey of Jeffrey Kagel, who leaves behind the possibility of a conventional music career and travels to India in search of something deeper. There, he encounters Neem Karoli Baba, known lovingly as Maharaj-ji, and begins a path that eventually leads him to become Krishna Das, one of the most beloved voices in modern kirtan and devotional music.

At its heart, this is a film about longing, heartbreak, devotion, music, and the search for what is real. It speaks to the ways life can break us open, the teachers and moments that change us, and the mystery of finding our way home through love.

After the screening, Jeremy will join us for a conversation about the film, the journey behind it, and the themes it opens up. There will also be space for community reflection and questions.

You do not need to know anything about kirtan, yoga, Hinduism, or meditation to attend. Come as you are.

**What to Expect**
We’ll gather, watch the film together, and then have a relaxed conversation with Jeremy Frindel. The space will be open, respectful, and rooted in the spirit of community. There is no pressure to share.

**[Please RSVP here](https://www.eventbrite.com/e/one-track-heart-the-story-of-krishna-das-screening-conversation-tickets-1993547622604?aff=oddtdtcreator)**

long_description:
Three days that change how connection feels in your body, your relationship, and your everyday life.

If intimacy feels like it belonged to a version of you who had more time, more ease, more fire…

And now it feels rushed. Scheduled. Negotiated.

You’re not broken.

You’re disconnected.

It's time to stop wondering where that part of you went.

Tantra is the gateway back to that version of you.

The version of you who felt:

more open

more confident

more present in your body

less guarded around touch, desire, and connection.

Tantra, in it's original form, was never about performance or technique alone.

It was an initiation into conscious love.

A discipline of awareness.

A sacred path that teaches how breath, attention, presence, and sexual energy shape connection itself.

This immersive retreat introduces both foundational and more advanced Tantric principles translated into a modern, trauma-informed framework grounded in neuroscience, somatic awareness, and relational psychology.

You will not simply learn techniques.

You will experience the deeper architecture of intimacy. You'll unlock how energy moves between bodies, how presence shapes arousal, how awareness transforms connection.

You’re not alone.

And you’re not broken.

For many people, intimacy doesn’t disappear.

It slowly becomes harder to access.

You start noticing things like:

Overthinking instead of feeling

Tension where there used to be ease

Desire that feels inconsistent or distant

Touch that feels expected instead of inviting

Connection that requires effort instead of happening naturally

This isn’t about chemistry.

It’s about nervous system safety.

And most of us were never taught how intimacy works in the body.

This Retreat Is About Changing How Intimacy Feels From The Inside Out

Whether you are single or partnered, intimacy begins with your ability to:

stay present instead of shutting down

receive without bracing

communicate desire without fear

experience pleasure without

long_description:
**This event is posted on behalf of the Westerly Land Trust. Registration is required outside of Meetup. [Please register here.](https://www.eventbrite.com/e/paddle-yoga-float-flow-registration-1993347180075)**

Certified yoga teacher, Janice Fifer, will guide us through Sun Salutations with a focus on hip and shoulder openers to prepare for a paddle up the Pawcatuck River. We will stop along the way for a short meditation and ride the river’s gentle current back to the put-in point. The day will end with relaxation and a closing circle. This is a moderate paddle for kayakers with some experience, with the emphasis on relaxing and enjoying nature.

**What to bring:** BYO Kayak, Paddle board, canoe etc, Paddle, Life Jacket, Yoga Mat, Large Towel (to put under your yoga mat), Water, Bug Repellent. Be aware that your shoes will get wet and muddy.

**Please note:** Rhode Island State Regulations require that everyone, regardless of age, MUST wear a US Coast Guard approved life jacket, fastened in the manner the manufacturer intended.

**Parking:** Parking is available at Flora Whitely Preserve at [197 Potter Hill Rd](https://www.google.com/maps/place/197+Potter+Hill+Rd,+Westerly,+RI+02891/@41.4137429,-71.7974699,21z/data=!4m5!3m4!1s0x89e5dd6e2199da8f:0xd825c68fe1fa552!8m2!3d41.4136666!4d-71.797423?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI2MDYyOS4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D "https://www.google.com/maps/place/197+Potter+Hill+Rd,+Westerly,+RI+02891/@41.4137429,-71.7974699,21z/data=!4m5!3m4!1s0x89e5dd6e2199da8f:0xd825c68fe1fa552!8m2!3d41.4136666!4d-71.797423?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI2MDYyOS4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D"). A Night of Enchanting Melodies: The Ali Azmat & Mustafa Zahid Junooni Tour
Get ready for an unforgettable night filled with the melodious tunes of Hindi and Urdu at the Ali Azmat & Mustafa Zahid Junooni Tour – Pakistan Independence Day Live in Concert! Scheduled to take place on the 15th of August, 2026, this will be a musical event like no other. The night will be filled with enchanting live performances, toe-tapping music, and an unforgettable party atmosphere as we come together to celebrate Pakistan's Independence Day in style. This is your chance to be part of a unique cultural experience that will captivate your senses and leave you yearning for more.
Meet the Maestros: Mustafa Zahid & Ali Azmat
We are thrilled to introduce you to our lead performers for the night – Mustafa Zahid and Ali Azmat. Ali Azmat is renowned across the globe as a singer-songwriter, musician, and actor. He hails from Pakistan and has an established career both as a solo artist and as the lead singer for the influential Sufi Rock band, Junoon. He made history in 2001 by becoming part of the first-ever Pakistani band to perform at the United Nations General Assembly. Joining him is Mustafa Zahid, celebrated as one of Pakistan's most versatile voices, known for his powerful vocals and chart-topping hits in both Bollywood and Pakistani music. Together, their soul-stirring music and compelling performances promise to mesmerize you at the Junooni Tour.
Experience the Magic at the Grand Center
The Junooni Tour will be hosted at the spacious and vibrant Grand Center, located at 300 Chisholm Pl, Plano, TX 75075. Known for its accessibility and a prime spot in the city, the venue provides ample parking for guests. Gates open at 8:00 PM, with the show starting at 8:30 PM. To make your evening more enjoyable, indulge in some delicious Pakistani and Indian cuisine at nearby restaurants before heading to the concert.
Secure Your Spot: Ticket Information
Make sure you don't miss out on this one-of-a-kind event! Our ticket structure accommodates everyone's budget and preference. Choose from 1st Row seating priced at $199, 2nd/3rd/4th Row seating for $99, and the Rest of the Seating available for $50. Book your tickets now and gear up for a night of incredible music, culture, and celebration as we honor Pakistan's Independence Day together.

long_description:
Join us for an uplifting evening of devotion and community at our Bhakti Kirtan, guided by the inspiring Subala Das! Immerse yourself in the soulful vibrations of mantra chanting, led by Subal and passionate kirtaniyas who bring the sacred sounds to life. Kirtan is a beautiful practice of call-and-response singing that opens the heart, uplifts the spirit, and connects us with the divine through the practice of bhakti.

Bhakti, a Sanskrit word meaning “devotion” or “love,” is the spiritual path of connecting with the divine through heartfelt surrender and loving service. It emphasizes cultivating a deep, personal relationship with the divine, often expressed through music, prayer, and acts of kindness. Bhakti transcends religious boundaries, welcoming everyone into its embrace of universal love.

This event is open to everyone, whether you’re new to kirtan or a seasoned practitioner. Come as you are and leave feeling nourished—body, mind, and soul. Bring your friends and family, and experience the joy of chanting and sharing a meal together in a warm and welcoming atmosphere!

long_description:
**BAPS Detroit Mandir 22nd Patotsav (Anniversary)**

Celebrate the 22nd anniversary of the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in the Detroit area, beautifully coinciding with India's Independence Day.

This grand celebration will feature:

- **2:00 PM** – Vedic Mahapuja (sacred fire ceremony)
- **2:00 – 5:00 PM** – Annakut Darshan (offering of hundreds of food items to the deities)
- **4:00 PM** – Patotsav Sabha (cultural assembly with addresses by visiting swamis)

The Patotsav marks the sacred anniversary of the mandir's murti pratishtha (consecration of the deities) and is one of the most auspicious events of the year.

**Details:**
- Date: Saturday, August 15, 2026
- Location: BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Canton, MI
- Admission: Free and open to all

Special prasad and celebrations throughout the day. All families welcome.

long_description:
This book club is still forming! If you're interested, get on the waitlist and I'll be in touch. Note that dates / times / location may change.

**A woman’s desperate flight from an Apache raid unfolds into a sweeping tale of the Mexico–US border wars.**

Orchestrated with a stunningly imagined cast of characters, both historical and purely fictional, *Now I Surrender* radically recasts the story of how the West was “won.” In the contested borderlands between Mexico and the United States, a woman flees into the desert after a devastating raid on her dead husband’s ranch. A lieutenant colonel in service to the fledgling Republic, sent in pursuit of cattle rustlers, discovers he’s on the trail of a more dramatic abduction. Decades later, with political ambitions on the line, the American and Mexican militaries try to maneuver Geronimo, the most legendary of Apache warriors, into surrender. In our own day, a family travels through the region in search of a truer version of the past.

Part epic, part alt-Western, *Now I Surrender* is Álvaro Enrigue’s most expansive and impassioned novel yet. It weaves past and present, myth and history into a searing elegy for a way of life that was an incarnation of true liberty—and an homage to the spark in us that still thrills to its memory.

title: The Great Exhale: A Journey from Movement to Stillness
description: The practice of coming to life is a celebration; the practice of letting go is a liberation. In this 60-minute practice, we honor the full spectrum of the human experience. We begin by fueling the fire within, moving through a vinyasa flow designed to build heat, find rhythm, and invite you into a s
long_description:
The practice of coming to life is a celebration; the practice of letting go is a liberation. In this 60-minute practice, we honor the full spectrum of the human experience. We begin by fueling the fire within, moving through a vinyasa flow designed to build heat, find rhythm, and invite you into a state of total presence. This is the INHALE—the vibrant, active effort of being fully alive.

As we reach the peak of our movement, we transition into the The Great EXHALE. We shift from the "doing" to the "being," laying it all down for an extended, soulful relaxation and meditation.

In this space, we practice the art of "dying" to the day, the ego, and the effort. By meeting this stillness with a sense of joy and curiosity, we discover that the end of the movement is not a loss, but an entry point into profound peace.

What to expect:

☮️ Vibrant Flow: A high-energy sequence with music to get you out of your head and into your body.

✌️ Deep Release: A long, guided Savasana (deep rest) to integrate the physical work.

🧘‍♂️ Joyful Stillness: A philosophical exploration of surrender as a path to great peace.

Guided by Lauren Barlag
